laws.rule: Mexico City's law protecting non-smokers bans smoking, and the use of vapes and similar devices, in enclosed places open to the public and other places the law lists. A smoker in a banned place can be fined by a civic judge.
laws.heading: Ley de Protección a la Salud de las Personas No Fumadoras de la Ciudad de México

laws.rule: Mexico City's civic culture law lists infractions that a civic judge handles. They include drinking alcohol in public places that aren't authorised, taking drugs in public, and selling alcohol on the street outside authorised fairs (Ley de Cultura Cívica, art. 28), and making noise that clearly disturbs other people's peace or risks health (art. 27). Sanctions are a fine of 1 to 40 times the UMA (the daily unit of account, MXN 117.31 in 2026, about A$8.87, so up to about MXN 4,692 or A$355), arrest of 6 to 36 hours, or community service (art. 31 sets bands by type of infraction). Rate: A$1 = about MXN 13.23.
laws.penalty_signal: Fine 1 to 40 UMA, or arrest up to 36 hours

laws.rule: Mexico City charges a lodging tax (Impuesto por la Prestación de Servicios de Hospedaje) on hotels, hostels, motels, timeshare and camping or caravan areas, and houses and apartments are also covered (Código Fiscal, art. 162). The rate is 3.5% of what the guest pays for hotel-type lodging (art. 164). The host collects it; platforms that take the payment must register and pay it (art. 162 Bis). Text held on OJN, last reform 30 December 2021.
